newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds seen rangebound ahead of US jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds seen rangebound ahead of US jobs data.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened largely unchanged on Thursday after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided, as expected, to leave interest rates steady.
Dealers expected the market to remain moribund at least until U.S. June unemployment figures were released at 1230 GMT.
"Up to the American jobless numbers the benchmark will trade within a 0.1 point range," a dealer said
At 0640 GMT the seven percent 2007 government bond, due officially to become the benchmark on September 1, was down 0.07 point from Tuesday's close, to 105.50 yielding 6.25 percent.
Its spread to the bund widened one basis point to 61 bp.
The crown was virtually unchanged at 3.8072 to the mark.

Dealers said that market sentiment was positive, a fact exploited by the central bank on Wednesday to sell around one billion crowns worth of paper all along the curve. The bank was expected to sell more on Thursday, they added.
